'''Joyce Mary Waters, Lady Waters''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|ONZM|size=85%}} (née '''Partridge'''; born 2 June 1931) is a New Zealand [[inorganic chemist]] and [[X-ray crystallographer]], who is currently professor emeritus at [[Massey University]]. She was the second woman to receive a [[PhD]] in chemistry at the University of Auckland, and the first woman to serve as president of the New Zealand Institute of Chemistry.

==Early life and family==
Waters was born Joyce Mary Partridge in [[Auckland]] on 2 June 1931, the daughter of Mary Elizabeth Partridge (née Harrison) and Thomas Harold Charles Partridge.<ref name="Whos who">{{cite book |editor-last=Taylor |editor-first=Alister |editor-link=Alister Taylor |title=New Zealand Who's Who Aotearoa 2001 |year=2001 |publisher=Alister Taylor Publishers |location=Auckland |issn=1172-9813 |page=922}}</ref> She was educated at [[Diocesan School for Girls, Auckland]], from 1938 to 1949, and went on to study at [[University of Auckland|Auckland University College]], graduating [[Bachelor of Science]] in 1954, [[Master of Science]] with first-class honours in 1955, and PhD in 1960.<ref name="Whos who"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://shadowsoftime.co.nz/university24.html |title=NZ university graduates 1870–1961: U–Wh |website=Shadows of Time |accessdate=7 September 2019}}</ref> The title of her doctoral thesis, supervised by [[John Llewellyn (academic)|John Llewellyn]] and [[David Hall (chemist)|David Hall]], was ''A study of some co-ordination compounds formed between nickel diammines and the nitrite ion''.<ref>{{cite thesis |last=Waters |first=Joyce |year=1960 |type=Doctoral thesis |title=A study of some co-ordination compounds formed between nickel diammines and the nitrite ion |publisher=ResearchSpace@Auckland, University of Auckland |hdl=2292/2160 |url=https://researchspace.auckland.ac.nz/handle/2292/2160}}</ref> She was the second woman to complete a PhD in chemistry at Auckland.<ref name="Suffrage 125">{{cite web |url=https://suffrage125science.auckland.ac.nz |title=Suffrage 125 – women in science |year=2018 |publisher=University of Auckland |accessdate=7 September 2019}}</ref>

In 1959, she married fellow inorganic chemist [[Neil Waters]], who was [[Knight Bachelor|knighted]] in 1995.<ref name="Whos who"/>

==Academic career==
Waters was appointed as a lecturer in chemistry at the University of Auckland in 1961, rising to the rank of associate professor.<ref name="Whos who"/> In 1983, she joined Massey University as a senior research fellow and associate professor in chemistry, and in 2000 she was made a full professor at Massey's Albany campus.<ref name="Whos who"/> Following her retirement, she was conferred with the title of professor emeritus.<ref name="Suffrage 125"/>

Her research focused on the determination of molecular structure using X-ray crystallography.<ref name="Whos who"/> An early publication by Waters was the first to describe the structure of a [[coordination complex]] containing a metal–hydrogen bond.<ref name="Suffrage 125"/>

Waters served as president of the New Zealand Institute of Chemistry in 1989–1990, and was the first woman to hold the position.<ref name="Whos who"/><ref name="Suffrage 125"/>

==Later life==
Following her formal retirement, Waters continued part-time research and teaching activities at Massey Albany.<ref name="Suffrage 125"/> Her husband, Neil Waters, died in Auckland in 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.massey.ac.nz/massey/about-massey/news/article.cfm?mnarticle_uuid=5B2C8267-57F4-4C26-A9FE-DCCB54529A16 |title=Former vice-chancellor Sir Neil Waters dies |date=14 June 2018 |publisher=Massey University |accessdate=8 September 2019}}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
In 1996, Waters was awarded the Massey Medal of Massey University, in recognition of services to the university and to science.<ref name="Whos who"/><ref>{{cite book |title=Massey University Calendar 2017 |url=https://sme-centre.massey.ac.nz/massey/fms/calendar/documents/2017/2017-Massey-University-Calendar.pdf?C04A8097106357DBCCCD5F01FE2AD716 |accessdate=8 September 2019 |year=2017 |publisher=Massey University |location=Palmerston North |page=51 |archive-date=31 January 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190131100535/https://sme-centre.massey.ac.nz/massey/fms/calendar/documents/2017/2017-Massey-University-Calendar.pdf?C04A8097106357DBCCCD5F01FE2AD716 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In the [[2006 New Year Honours (New Zealand)|2006 New Year Honours]], she was appointed an [[Officer of the New Zealand Order of Merit]], for services to chemistry.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.dpmc.govt.nz/publications/new-year-honours-list-2006 | title=New Year honours list 2006 |date=31 December 2005 | publisher=Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet | accessdate=8 September 2019}}</ref>

Waters was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of New Zealand]] in 1999,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org.nz/who-we-are/our-people/our-fellows/all-fellows/v-z/ |title=List of all Fellows with surnames V–Z |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |accessdate=8 September 2019}}</ref> and is also a Fellow of the New Zealand Institute of Chemistry.<ref name="Whos who"/>
